html:
SMTO-MEM-0030 — SMTO couldn't find that passage in the document

GUID: 0b1d7a6a-6caf-5a7d-bbd5-95248dbc3b81
Slug: knowledge-invalid-reference
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to open a passage using a link it couldn't follow. The link was cut short, typed in the wrong form, or pointed past the end of the document. Your documents weren't changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the link came from an Agent answer, ask the Agent the question again so it searches your documents and gives new source links. New links are built straight from the current search results, so they point to passages that exist.
  2. If you copied or typed the link yourself, don't edit it. Open the source link again from the answer it came from. A link that is cut short or changed by hand no longer points to a real passage.
  3. To check the passages yourself, open Knowledge, go to Test retrieval, choose the conversation, type your question and select Search. The results there link to passages that exist in each document right now.

What success looks like

  • The source link opens and shows the passage text.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which answer or link you used. Don't delete or replace the document to fix this; the document itself is fine.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • RagService.fetch rejected the source reference because it was not in document:version:passage form, its passage number was outside the document's passage list, or the requested neighbors value was outside 0 to 2.

What this means

  • The saved link does not identify an available source in this request. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported invalid_reference. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The selected source opens successfully.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Use a reference exactly as returned by POST /api/agent/rag/search or the rag.search tool: document_id:generation:chunk_index, with chunk_index inside that generation's chunk list and neighbors between 0 and 2. The rejected fetch modified nothing; re-run the search rather than editing or constructing references by hand.
  • Refresh the source list and select the source again. Keep unsaved note text before changing the selection.

Retry and execution caution

  • The selected source opens successfully.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected source opens successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
